My uncle has Down syndrome and will turn 50 next year. Because special ed was essentially nonexistent in Utah, he’s unable to read and he has really limited independence. It’s been 20 years since my grandmother underwent intensive cancer treatment and passed away. Ever since then, all the siblings have had to pull together to make sure he has a house to live in and a stable schedule where he can get to and from work and everything. There’s been a lot of sacrifice while everyone has families of their own to tend to. Over the past year, we’ve seen a sharp decline in his cognitive health that comes with erratic moods and outbursts of rage where he sometimes hurts himself or others. Now the family is faced with deciding what to do going forward for an indefinite amount of time. It’s definitely easy to make them villains, especially for the damaging rhetoric they’ve been spreading, but some people need to come down from their ivory towers and understand that providing good quality of life for someone with Down syndrome can be a multigenerational effort.
